summary: Used the remaining budget for one independent, bounded source check outside the feature audited so far: the network transport's heartbeat fast path, which calls the Raft heartbeat handler from the transport goroutine instead of the main loop. The guard is conservative — a decoded AppendEntries request is treated as a heartbeat only when it has a non-zero term, a leader address, zero PrevLogEntry and PrevLogTerm, no entries and a zero LeaderCommitIndex — and the handler accepts only AppendEntries and returns immediately on shutdown, so that off-main-loop path cannot append entries or apply committed entries, and no claim can be built on it. I recorded that as a sourced negative (three source ranges, one behavior entry) rather than leaving an unexamined suspicion, noting that the in-memory transport used by the harnesses has no fast path, so the check does not affect any receipt. No conclusion in the run changes: the parent question and its two dependent questions remain explained with their defect claims asserted, the constructor question remains explained with the stall reachable at default batch settings through tolerated snapshot failures, all receipts are cited, no question has an open necessary gap, and the remaining items are the recorded limits (single harness-issued membership change, entry-count long run, harness-arranged lag for the per-node repair, self-produced snapshot for the restore, an injected Create-failure store for the stall, in-memory stores with scaled timeouts and bounded observation windows).
